You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Federation The universe is organized into many federations which trade, intrigue, develop… One of these federations, still not fully developed yet (5 member planets so far) wants a new delegation to join them, but you are not the only one having your sights set on the federation. The Federation challenges you to prove your worth for 5 years. During these 5 years, you must develop strategies, deploy tactics, take the best opportunities but also form the right alliances at the right time… In the end, only 1 delegation will be chosen: the one with the most prestige! Federation is played over 5 rounds. Each round is divided into 2 main steps. The first step is player turns where each player plays an Ambassador's pawn and send a spaceship on a special mission. Once all players have completed their turn, the Executive Phase starts, where players receive their income, fund Major Projects and pass laws. At the end of the 5th round, the game ends. The Player with the most prestige points wins the game and joins the Federation. In case of a tie, the victory is shared. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 51 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Federation and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Rounds 4 Ambassador's Phase 5 Executive Phase 6 End of Round 7 End of Game 8 Additional Notes Overview Have the most prestige points (PP) after 5 rounds Setup In reverse turn order, choose a starting bonus Rounds Each round is split into two phases Ambassador's Phase (Played 4 times per round) Executive Phase (Played once after all Ambassador phases) Ambassador's Phase On your turn, Place one of your four tokens on a still-vacant space from among the 18 spaces in the senate, either Voting side or Funding side up Voting -side-up tokens have numbers from 1-3; these represent the votes you have cast in: -- The left or right side of the senate -- The floor (top, middle, or bottom) of the senate Funding -side-up tokens immediately gain you any crystal shown, as well as making available to you the special mission on your player board that corresponds to the space you covered in the senate. Alteration Tokens : If you have an Alteration Token (usually gained from the blue '6moon' planet), you can combine it with a token before you place it to increase or change the power or bonus of the token. Voting Alternation Tokens must go with Voting-side-up tokens, and Funding Alteration Tokens must go with Funding-side-up tokens. Assistant Die: If you use your voting side, you can add your assistant die (if non-zero) to the token when placing it, to increase your votes. Medals of Honour: If your action was on any of the five coloured planets, you will earn a medal of honour if you are the first person to reach level 3 influence on that planet. If somebody else has reached level 3, you must reach level 4 influence to gain a medal of honour, and so on. These medals go on the bottom of your scoring area and you will earn VPs at the end equal to the number shown to the right of your most recent medal. You can only gain one in each colour. Special Mission : Optionally, after resolving your token placement, if you have any fighters available, you can place them on any available special mission on your player board, resolving it. In addition to having activated the mission by placing a funding-side-up token on the corresponding space, your Accreditation Marker (left hand side of player board) must be at the same level as the special mission. Voting versus Funding : essentially, you are choosing between casting voting power to gain end-of-round PPs for majorities the side of the senate and each of the three floors (see below), or using the funding side to earn crystals, unlock special missions, and fund the projects at the top of each column in the senate: if these are successfully funded, they will pay out VPs to the players with most influence in that area at the end of the game. [Rating: 1/10] This is the first time I don't want to play a game after the rules explanation. I tried to play but as I thought, it was REALLY BAD !!! The worst "expert game" I played for years (and I love expert games generally speaking). The theme is totally pasted-on and the game as a lot of micro-rules that don't go well together like the ones in a Lacerda game for example. The first game isn't really interesting because you don't know what's going on and the game is complex for nothing. This game could be studied in a designer school as "what not to do" ! [Rating: 3/10] Too heavy for me and too deterministic, need a little more luck in my games to give me a chance.

[Rating: 3/10] There is basically nothing for me to like in this game. The actions are uninteresting, the world-building is uninteresting, the scoring is point-salady. A typical abstract euro, convoluted for the sake of convolutedness: you need C to do B, and B helps doing A, and D will give you points, and cycle back. Themeless and uninspired.

[Rating: 3/10] Federation is heavy for the sake of heavy, with an unbearable amount of components.  It uses double-sided worker discs to tie worker placement in with voting, in a way that genuinely works.  For all the different weighty aspects of Federation, it all holds together quite well.  Medals are a way to score points in the game, and obtaining them is a race.  When one player gets a medal, the threshold for an opponent to get the same medal increases. [Rating: 3.5/10] Did not go onto my watchlist, but after many praises and a friend who bought it, I had a chance to play it.  Away from the group that completely turned into AP mode, what an uninspired piece of spreadsheet... boring and dry as hell with nothing interesting happening, while you go through tons of icons that don't fit well. Nothing original in here, but alot of rules (some just to get other rules working...). Pretty much the very opposite of what I want from a game.  There are sooo many much better WP games out there, no need for this complicated and very fiddly one.

[Rating: 4/10] Far too much going on to be fun. More =/= better. Streamline the actions and options for a more sensical game.

[Rating: 4/10] Tenía muchas ganas de probarlo por su estética y porque le veía mucho potencial a su mecánica principal, pero la primera partida me ha dejado gélido. La ejecución del diseño me parece arbitraria y poco coherente, con una altísima influencia del azar para lo largas que son las partidas.

[Rating: 4/10] This is where eurogames jump the shark for me. 32 pages of rules. Almost 4 hours for a learning game for 4 experienced gamers. It's an impressive, well-tested design and the components are lovely. It's just too much.

[Rating: 4/10] It's hard to find much to love here. Some of the worst trappings of area-control games surround the central parliament, which initially promises something original and interesting, but ultimately fails to deliver.
